findings.F1: In coins whose 90-day return is not negative, the 5-day unusual move after a day's rise grows with the rise measured in 20-day standard deviations: −0.77 % (t −2.08, 1092 cases) for 0–1 units, +1.42 % (t 1.77, 247) for 1–1.5, +2.31 % (t 2.29, 163) for 1.5–2 and +8.58 % (t 2.65, 134; winsorised +5.91 %, t 4.05; median +2.35 %, 66 % of cases positive) above 2, a strength of 0.55 of the coin's usual 5-day move in the top bucket.
findings.F2: That grading in rising coins is steady across years and coins: over the 1636 rising-coin up-day cases, the Spearman correlation of the rise with the 5-day unusual move is 0.124 and stays between 0.10 and 0.14 when any one year is left out; 17 of 19 coins have a positive median after rises above 1.5 units; averaged per day it is still +4.65 % with t 2.31 over 126 independent days.
findings.F3: The fade that the tested idea relies on does not hold up. In falling coins, rises above 2 units are followed by −3.77 % over 5 days (t −2.72, 79 cases), but one year carries it: −12.9 % (t −6.34, 24 cases) in 2025 against +7.6 % (t 3.15) in 2021 and +2.2 % in 2023. Averaged per day it is only −1.07 % (t −0.68, 71 days), and the correlation of the rise with the next 5 days' move is −0.04 to −0.08.
findings.F4: The book loses on the coins' drift and not on its timing: per bar the position earns −0.0112 %, of which −0.0294 % is the market's own rise against a short held on 44 % of the bars, while timing adds +0.0182 %. That matches step 5's size: total move −0.14 % per case against a cost of 0.22 %.
findings.F5: Among rising coins with a rise above 1 unit, the following 5-day move is larger the larger the 90-day gain: −0.91 % for a 90-day gain of 0–20 %, +0.74 % for 20–50 %, +2.51 % for 50–100 % and +16.7 % above 100 % (winsorised t 2.54, 40 cases). This is suggestive only, on few cases.
findings.F6: Two other patterns did not survive averaging per day, so I give them no weight. The rebound after a 90-day fall of more than 50 % (+3.15 %, t 2.62, 139 cases) drops to t 0.16 over 41 days. The weekday pattern of next-day moves has every weekday's |t| below 1.91 once averaged per day.

ideas.idea: In a coin whose 90-day return is positive, a one-day rise that is large relative to its usual daily move (its 20-day standard deviation of daily returns) is followed by a further rise over the next 5 days, and the larger that rise in units of the usual daily move, the larger the rise that follows.
ideas.consequence: A sharp up day in a coin that has been rising for months is a reason to be long for the following days rather than to fade it, with more weight the sharper the day.
ideas.name: rising-coin breakouts keep going
